title: A protocol for detecting elemental calcium signals (Ca2+ puffs) in mammalian cells using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy
protocol: Pre-warm cell culture media, DPBS, trypsin, and poly-D-lysine by placing them in a water bath set to 37°C.
Place pre-autoclaved 15 mm No1 coverslips in each well of a 12-well cell culture plate using tweezers.
Add 0.1–0.2 ml poly-D-lysine/well of the 12-well plate to coat the coverslips sufficiently.
Incubate the coated coverslips for 1 hour at room temperature (25°C) in a laminar flow cabinet.
Remove poly-D-lysine and rinse each well three times with DPBS.
Leave the plates uncovered for at least 1 hour in the laminar flow cabinet to dry.
Seed 0.5 x 10^6 cells in each well of a 12-well plate containing poly-D-lysine-coated coverslips.
Add 1 ml cell culture media to each seeded well and leave plates in an incubator for 48 hours.
View the cells under a microscope using brightfield illumination after 48 hours to ensure cells have adhered and attained flattened morphology.
Prepare 5 μM Cal-520-AM by dissolving 5 μL of 1 mM Cal-520-AM in 1 mL imaging buffer with 1% BSA.
Prepare 1 μM ci-IP3-PM by dissolving 1 μL of 1 mM ci-IP3-PM in 1 mL imaging buffer with 1% BSA.
Transfer cells on coverslip from step (a) into a 35-mm dish in the laminar flow cabinet using fine-tip forceps.
Wash the coverslip gently three times with 750 μL of imaging buffer.
Incubate the coverslip in 750 μL of Cal-520-AM and ci-IP3-PM supplemented imaging buffer at 25°C for an hour.
Rinse the coverslip gently with imaging buffer three times following incubation.
Prepare 5 μM EGTA-AM by dissolving 5 μL of 10 mM EGTA in 10 mL imaging buffer.
Add 750 μL of EGTA-AM supplemented imaging buffer to the coverslip and incubate at 25°C for 45 minutes.
Rinse the coverslip gently with imaging buffer three times following incubation.
Incubate the coverslip in fresh imaging buffer at 25°C for another 45 minutes.
Attach the coverslip to a Warner perfusion chamber using fine forceps and vacuum grease.
Image at least five coverslips for each experimental set using TIRF microscopy.
Add 1 mL imaging buffer to the perfusion chamber.
Clean the bottom of the cover slip using a kimwipe.
Place a drop of low autofluorescence immersion oil on the Olympus IX81 inverted microscope equipped with PlanApo 60x/1.45 Oil TIRFM Microscope Objective.
Fasten the Warner perfusion chamber onto the microscope stage.
Use Olympus CellSens Dimensions 2.3 software for imaging.
Select appropriate objective, laser, and TIRF settings in the acquisition software.
Control camera parameters including exposure time, gain, resolution, and field of view/region of interest.
Adjust laser and LED intensity to illuminate dye-loaded cells.
Adjust display to optimize appearance of dye loaded cells.
Create, save, and execute a protocol for image acquisition using the experiment manager window.
Define commands including laser type, exposure time, UV laser shutter control, and recording time.
Acquire a three-second baseline prior to photolysis.
Deliver UV flash from a 405 nm laser for 1 second (photolysis of ci-IP3).
Record Ca2+ puffs for 40 seconds using the 488 nm laser.
Optimize angle of incidence of laser to achieve total internal reflection by adjusting the angle offset in the TIRF adjustment window.
Excite Cal-520 indicator using a 488 nm laser (set the intensity to a minimum such that the indicator fluorescence does not photobleach).
Ensure that the cells are in focus and in the incident angle of the laser achieves TIRF.
Set the protocol in the software to record baseline for at least 3/5 seconds.
Deliver a UV-flash using a 405 nm laser uniformly to uncage ci-IP3 for 1 second.
Alternatively, focus the UV laser light to a spot to illuminate a region of a cell.
Record the Ca2+ puffs for a user-defined time period following uncaging.
Capture emitted fluorescence using a Hamamatsu ORCA-fusion CMOS digital camera C14440.
Ensure all necessary precautions are considered before operating lasers.
Wear appropriate goggles and long-sleeve gloves during laser operation.
Keep lights off during the entire imaging process.
Set the 488 nm laser intensity to a minimum.
Confirm optimum laser intensity for imaging using HEK-3KO cells.
Optimize UV flash intensity typically in the range of 0.1–2 mW and duration between 100 ms–1000 ms.
Enhance recording speed by increasing binning to 4 × 4.
Avoid photobleaching/spontaneous puff activity during imaging.
Use HEK-3KO cells for confirming optimal laser intensity settings.
Ensure cells appear healthy after dye loading.
Acquire images for at least ∼45 min following dye loading.
Reuse each coverslip multiple times for acquiring recordings.
Limit exposure of the same field to UV-laser light to avoid repeated recording from the same area.
Convert .vsi files into .tif format using Image J.
Load the .tif file in FLIKA software.
Crop the loaded image to accommodate a single cell.
Trim frames to be analyzed.
Select Process – Math – Subtract on the graphical user interface (for example 450, black levels).
Select the subtracted window and choose Process – Math – Ratio by Baseline.
Set First frame to 0, Number of frames to 290, Ratio Type to Average, Black Level to 0.00.
Filter the ratioed data using Butterworth filter settings: Filter order 3, Low cutoff Frequency (e.g., 2), High cutoff Frequency (e.g., 10), Frame rate (Hz) (e.g., 97 fps).
Select the Ratioed by Average – Butter Filtered window.
Process – Math – Ratio by Baseline with settings: First frame – 0, Number of frames – 290, Ratio Type – standard deviation, Black Level – 0.00.
Normalize the baseline to 0.
Select the Ratioed by average – butter filtered – Ratioed by standard deviation window.
Process – Filter – Gaussian Blur with Sigma (pixels) set to 3, normalized edges, preview set to true.
Adjust the histogram for puff detection.
Create a Gaussian Blurred normalized window.
Plugins – Detect Puffs – Threshold cluster.
Select appropriate windows (A, B, C).

Enter Roi_width value (e.g.: 5), paddingXY (e.g.: 20), padding_pre (e.g.: 20), padding_post (e.g.: 20), maxSigma For GaussianFit (e.g.: 90), radius (e.g.: 5), maxPuffDiameter (e.g.: 30), blur_thresh (e.g.: 1), time_factor (e.g.: 2).
Load_flika_file set to false.
Rotatedfit set to true.
Set Blur Threshold with a desired value (e.g.: 1.00).
Hit set threshold button.
Right click and circle the clusters.
Fit Gaussian.
In control panel, monitor individual puffs and adjust start and end of individual puff.
Export details about events assigned to clusters to excel.
Plot amplitudes of Ca2+ puffs in hR1 endo cells.
Create a scatter plot depicting the number of puff sites/cell and puffs/cell.
Determine mean-rise (r) and -fall (f) times for fluorescence changes.
Save the experimental parameters in a (.flika) file for future references.
Optimize the parameters based on cell types, recording speed, number of puffs, frequency of puffs, duration of puff, and radius of puffs.
Manually confirm all puffs identified automatically by the algorithm before analysis.
